chapters.title: Chapter 151: Blame Shifting
paragraphs: "Kekeke, Nine Pacts has your demon cores—take them if you dare." Blunder laughed loudly. He enjoyed this messy situation.
Demon Generals against Nine Pacts and Bone Blood Cult.
Nine Pacts against Vritra, Demon Generals, and Bone Blood Cult.
Bone Blood Cult against everyone.
"So both of you were in on this together. Looks like I’ll have to do the questioning with your corpses." Thaddeus roared as he took out a large metallic bat shaped staff.

His body began to transform in the next moment, his muscles bulging and enlarging at an alarming rate, as his veins wiggled like worms. His body soon became more than twenty feet in height, and his face resembled a bull as his round horns became even more deadly, glowing with a bright white light.
"Cover this place. No one is allowed to leave from this moment on." Morvik said.
"What about those carriages?" Silquor questioned, as he pulled out a magical staff from the air and began to wave it around.

"They are just insignificant humans. It doesn’t matter what happens to them. They will end up dead in a battle of this level anyway." Morvik spoke as he removed his worn out clothes and stored them away carefully, now only wearing the white cloth that covered his entire body.

His body twisted and wriggled in the air, slowly transforming into an enormous insect with several large wings on its back and countless feet that had sharp tips. The white clothes were torn to pieces as the gigantic insect towered over every person present.
"Keke, that transformation of yours is always so ugly—it completely breaks your cool act." Silquor laughed as he created a large dome around the forest, completely locking everyone inside.
The three Demon Generals were ready to slaughter most of the people present in this vicinity. Their only goal was to find the real thief and get back the core.
"Are you sure you want the Nine Pacts as your enemy?" Faceless asked, his voice as calm as ever.

The Nine Pacts’ members might be much weaker than the Demon Generals, but they weren’t afraid. If the higher ups of their organization learned of this, then these three Demon Generals who had lost their lord would be hunted until the end of the world.
Silquor, Thaddeus, and Morvik were aware of all this as well, so they weren’t even planning to use half of their power. And they also couldn’t kill a high ranked member of the Nine Pacts.

But it was different with the Bone Blood Cult, who were enemies to most organizations. Most people depended on themselves there—even if all these people were killed here, there was a high chance that no one would even come to take revenge.

’But if these lunatics have decided to challenge us on their own despite knowing the risks, then they must have planned something. Even this location is chosen by them. They are definitely up to something.’ Morvik warned the other two through telepathy, a skill that people at higher levels could do easily.
"Hahaha, since all of us are getting started, why don’t you make your appearance now? Won’t it be too bad to die as a no name?" Blunder looked at the carriage and spoke out loud.
The twenty guards and the two coachmen were frightened out of their wits when they saw the horrific scene in the sky.
Thousands of men in blood red dress, thousands of men in black dress, three extremely powerful demons hovered in the air—and all the eyes suddenly focused on the carriages.

The horses neighed and almost collapsed under the huge pressure brought just by the gaze of all those people, as finally the carriages stopped moving. For a few seconds there was complete silence except for the wind blowing through the thick forest.
Drrrrrrr...
Then the door to the second carriage opened slowly before Vritra stepped outside, his face emotionless.
{Sin Point Gained: Watched +22,998}

After stepping out of the carriage, Vritra gazed up at all the participants of this battle as he closed the door behind him. Then he looked at the coachmen and said, "If you wish to survive, then move as far away from here as you can."

The two coachmen were frozen in fear, but Vritra’s words seemed to bring them back to reality. They looked at the spherical dome covering the large space, then looked back at him and asked, "S- Sir, what about you?"
"..." Vritra didn’t respond and turned his eyes away. The two coachmen gritted their teeth as they pulled the reins of their horses and tried to move close to the boundary of the dome.
"Hey hey, we can’t have that now, can we? What would be the fun in letting them just watch the fight and not participate?" Blunder’s twisted smile became visible from above the mask.
Once he selected a target, he would bring every kind of torture upon him. And what would be better than killing his small family right in front of him while he watched carefully?

And for some reason, Vritra seemed much more interesting than any of his past ’targets.’ He wanted to enjoy seeing him show emotions like pain, despair, begging—before he would die in the battle between the three organizations.
Of course, if he really managed to somehow survive this, then Vritra would be the best toy in the world.

Because of Blunder’s high interest in Vritra, he had even sent a few people to keep an eye on the carriages at all times. Those following Vritra were two of the people that worked directly under him out of the nine others—their strength was no joke.

They had seen one of the carriages separate from the other two. At first they thought Vritra might be sending his family separately, but that carriage was completely empty. Just to be sure, they got rid of it after it had traveled some distance.
That was how Blunder knew that Vritra had no time or opportunity to send his family away yet. That poor lamb probably hadn’t even predicted that all of a sudden so many enemies would be upon him.
That was why, even though Blunder couldn’t sense the presence of the carriages—which were covered by a barrier by Yasmine—he knew all the people Vritra loved and cared for were right here.

"Hmmm..." Vritra ran his gaze over Blunder before looking at the armies. Then he muttered, "You are fewer in numbers than I thought. I guess the Golden Moon has not arrived yet. And you must be the one I sensed under the king’s bed that day, right?"
Every action and word from Vritra brought him thousands of sin points, though he didn’t really like this kind of situation.

"Oh?" Blunder’s eyes widened slightly in surprise—not only because of the calmness Vritra displayed, but also the fact that he was able to draw all these conclusions with so little knowledge. Certainly, he wasn’t simple.

"Hahaha, that was indeed me. You surprised me a bit by appearing out of nowhere. Despite being at such a low level, you have such high control over space—one of the rarest ’Fields.’ After reaching the Legion rank, your strength will definitely explode." Blunder’s laugh reverberated across the entire place.

chapters.title: Chapter 152: Dead end
paragraphs: "And I would have loved to invite you to join the Bone Blood Cult, but what a pity—you caught my interest, and now I can’t help but want to break you," Blunder said, while the others waited.
The three demon generals were in no hurry to start the battle just yet. The more others fought, the better it would be for them. This way, they could even obtain more information.
"So you are the one who killed everyone at the Nine Pacts’ base? You are quite weak. Did you get someone else’s help?"
Faceless took a step forward in the air as he looked curiously at Vritra. He couldn’t sense anything special about him except his good looks and perfect build.

"Yes, I was indeed one of the participants who took part in killing several thousand cannon fodders of the Nine Pacts. As for the other one..." Vritra looked at Blunder, who was still smiling hideously, and pointed.

"I cooperated with him. He wanted to draw the stronger members of the Nine Pacts to this place for some reason. I remember him talking about his plan to kill some generals or something... and even something about a core."

As Vritra spoke, all eyes moved toward Blunder with doubt. Of course, they wouldn’t just believe a random person’s words, but now it made more sense. The Bone Blood Cult might have been behind this from the start.

The Nine Pacts, who were here to perform their experiments and search for a treasure, were suddenly slaughtered by a no name person. It was obvious that a stronger team would arrive to replace the dead and also to kill the person responsible for it all.
Wouldn’t this be the perfect way for the Bone Blood Cult to use them however they wished?

As for the three demon generals, their Demon Lord’s core was stolen. They were mad and only seeing red— just a bit of pointing, and they would slaughter their way through like bulls. And at the start, the Bone Blood Cult did make the Nine Pacts and demon generals enemies.
The Bone Blood Cult even planned to involve the Golden Moon, just as Vritra had said at the start, but they seemed to be running late— so they wouldn’t be part of this plan.

"Hahaha," Blunder hugged his belly and laughed out loud. It seemed his new target was quite clever too. He was so easily turning all the attention back at him and, while mixing the truth and lies, making them the cause of everything— even in the things they hadn’t done, like stealing the demon core.
"Good, good, you are much better than I thought. Ahhh~ This is going to be so much fun. More, more— show me more of what you are capable of," Blunder said out loud.
Though both he and Vritra knew no words could make him safe in such a situation. Not to mention just the Nine Pacts— he would die just from the aftershocks of the battle.
’Yasmine, what are the chances of us escaping from this place?’ Vritra asked while the others were busy with their own thoughts.

"I can’t teleport out of this tomb, and even your fourth dimension won’t work here. The space inside the dome is as if it has been completely separated from the outside world, so you would meet a wall even in your fourth dimension," Yasmine replied in a solemn tone.
’And what are the chances of my survival?’ he asked another question.

"..." Yasmine couldn’t answer that instantly. After all, it was just impossible to get out of there alive. But then she added, "If worst comes to worst, I will make a part of the dome explode with my soul power, and then we would have a chance at escaping."

’There’s no way we can go along with that option. That’s too dangerous and the chances of success are too low— not to mention I can’t put you in danger,’ Vritra said before asking, ’Can you tell me how strong they exactly are? What are their levels?’

"Yes, I can tell you, but with your current level you won’t be able to remember that info anyway. The Gods put various rules over the people— unless you’ve reached the Legion rank, you won’t be able to remember their level.
But I can tell you that every person here is above level two thousand, or at least that is how much strength they are going to use right now. Otherwise, they might get themselves into trouble.

Those three generals, those ten from the Bone Blood Cult, and those five from the Nine Pacts— all of them will be using combat power around level two thousand," Yasmine explained, and Vritra was definitely quite shocked upon hearing that.
But he quickly got over his surprise. After all, he never intended to win in the first place against all these monsters.
It was a good thing that the three demon generals were not yet aware that he was the thief they were looking for. Otherwise, all three organizations would attack just him.
"If you have anything more to say, you can go ahead. This might be the biggest achievement of your life," Blunder said.
He didn’t seem afraid or bothered by Vritra’s words. Except for the stealing of the core, everything else was true, after all. He did want everyone to gather here so he could kill them.

"..." Vritra stood silent, no emotion on his face as he stared back at all the figures in the sky. Previously, he felt a bit nervous, but now that he was face to face with death, he didn’t really feel anything.
He just had one simple plan— die at the start of the battle and act dead until it ends, and if even a little of his body is preserved, then he could be revived after the battle ends.
So, he just needs to stay dead during the entirety of the battle, he doubted those people would be interested in a corpse of a low level person.
Yasmine would never agree to such a plan— how could she just watch him die? But that was the best option for now, with its own possible risks.

"Well, we don’t have all the time in the world, so why don’t we get the party started with the holy sacrifice of the goddess, your mother, and your lover? I want to see how you will act when you’re desperate." Blunder said, as his face became extremely unsightly. He loved this part more than anything. This type of pain could make a person go crazy even more than any kind of physical pain. Most of his targets went crazy when they watched their family die at his hands— though there were also a few who easily gave them up to save their lives.
"..." Vritra glared at Blunder, dust swirling around his body as he activated one of his new skills.
[Activated Suck! Suck! Suck!]
Instead of going all out, he just breathed in energy through his nose, which would keep his energy reserves full even if he expended almost all of it in an instant.

Blunder made a grabbing motion in the air, as a bloody liquid appeared around the second carriage. It twisted and increased in size and soon became a large blood hand that grabbed the entire carriage with those thick, bloody fingers.

chapters.title: Chapter 153: The Unpaid Debt
paragraphs: The demon generals and the Nine Pacts didn’t interrupt, but they had no interest in someone as weak as Vritra. The Nine Pacts’ work would be done after he is dead, so even if he dies at Blunder’s hand, they won’t really mind.
As for the demon generals, they used this time to find what was making the Bone Blood Cult so confident. There had to be something that made them believe they could handle everyone here.

"Now beg, show me your best performance. Watch and plead as you watch everyone you care for die at my hands, haaah~ so exciting." Blunder said in a rather perverse tone, as the bloody hand grabbed the carriage.
Blunder had one of his hands raised as he grabbed the empty air while his eyes were fixed on Vritra’s expression, waiting to see that change—the change to satisfy his twisted desires.

As the carriage rose high into the air, the coachman jumped off hastily and ran towards the other carriage, praying to every god there is to survive this disaster. He was an ordinary man in his fifties.
CREAAAKKKKK
The carriage began to shake wildly under the pressure of the bloody hand. Vritra’s eyes widened in shock as he raised both hands and formed a hand of dust just as big in size.
Blunder’s face twisted even more in satisfaction as he sensed the desperation in Vritra’s action. But the dust hand crumbled the moment it struck the hand of blood—the power difference was too big.
"Sigh, fine, go ahead and do it, you monster." Vritra just turned his gaze away from the gruesome scene that was about to follow. He couldn’t bring himself to watch such destruction.

"Hmm..." Blunder raised an eyebrow, not expecting him to give up so easily. He tilted his head slightly and exerted some pressure, as the carriage began to bend and a loud creaking and thudding sound was produced.
But Vritra still didn’t react. He only clenched his fists and shut his eyes tight, enduring the pain.
BANG
Blunder exerted more force as the carriage was crushed and everything inside it became rubble. The barrier that Yasmine had formed over it was destroyed as well.
"..." Blunder waited for the painful cries to come, but there was utter silence. Finally, he locked his senses on the broken carriage—and there wasn’t a single drop of blood nor any corpses inside.
He looked back at the two men who had been ordered to follow Vritra. The level of these two people was also well above two thousand, so there was absolutely no way they would make any mistake.
"Come forward." He said after letting go of the carriage, which fell down with a loud boom. The luxurious carriage was destroyed just like that.

"Y-Yes sir." The two men in red clothes were shivering; they were even more baffled. From the moment Vritra had left the temple, they had kept an eye on him all the way up to here, not missing a single moment.
The three women had been with him until this morning when he opened the windows, but now there was no one inside.

"Did the carriage disappear from your sight for even a moment?" Blunder asked, his tone emotionless. But rage was building up inside him. He was about to enjoy such a good show—but now it was gone just like that.

"N-NO sir, we kept watch over him the entire time. We didn’t take a break for even a moment." One of the two men knelt in the air before the other followed. They were crazy, but not nearly as much as Blunder.

"Hmm, I see. Good job. You deserve an award. So right under your noses, this weak little toy who hasn’t even arrived at the legion rank yet made the three fully grown women disappear, and you had no idea about it?" Blunder asked, his lips stretching into a kind smile.

"S-Sir, all this time we didn’t n-notice any kind of change. The carriages progressed just as usual. At one point, one of the carriages did separate from the others, but I got rid of it and made sure no one was inside it. I really d-don’t understand when it happened." One of the two men explained.

"Sigh, you are lucky. If this wasn’t such an important occasion, then I would have dealt with you both first. Stand up and return to your positions. Your punishment will come soon." Blunder waved his hand as the two men took their positions.

’From what I have seen of him, he would have definitely beaten the two to a pulp for making such a big mistake—yet he didn’t right now, which means he needs them all for his next plan, and they need to be at certain positions...’ Vritra pondered, an unusual habit of his to observe the surroundings.
But he soon gave up. It wouldn’t matter what he thinks or plans, those people are way too strong and no trick would work against them.
If he really wished to beat them right now, then he probably would need to be born again.

"Sigh, that took away all the fun. I thought before the actual battle I could have a delicious appetizer, but I guess you are too smart—" Blunder shook his head. He was quite impressed by Vritra’s capability and felt more reluctant to just directly kill him.
Wouldn’t it be much better to slowly kill this great toy? And he might really get the chance to kill those women in front of him in the future.
But Blunder’s words were interrupted by Vritra’s loud shout:
"You think you can scare me just because you are a bit stronger? If you weren’t born so long before me then you would be nothing in front of me. Just wait—I’m going to kill you with my hands."

"Wait, what are you planning to do? You can’t fight them. I am going to create a disturbance in the barrier now, and then you could escape through the hole." Yasmine spoke. She gathered all her energy, even her soul energy, to create one powerful attack and blast a part of the barrier.

’Heh, don’t think you can just escape from your debt so easily. You owe me so many spanks. Before I take my revenge for all the teasing, I am not going to let you leave. So just rest for a while—I will take care of everything.’ Vritra spoke in a playful tone before he completely locked Yasmine with his authority over her.

All the energy she had gathered dispersed instantly and she couldn’t come out of his body. Yasmine was shocked, but she struggled to come out. How could she leave him with all those monsters, all alone, only to suffer at their hands?

Darkness appeared all around Yasmine and even her voice was drowned. She couldn’t do anything no matter how much she tried. Her eyes welled up with tears for the first time since the death of her parents. She screamed and pleaded and desperately tried to come out—but to no avail.
Vritra looked at Blunder as all emotions disappeared from his eyes and only bloodlust remained, a storm of dust began to swirl in the surrounding as his body rose into the air.

sentences.text: The demon generals and the Nine Pacts didn’t interrupt, but they had no interest in someone as weak as Vritra.
The Nine Pacts’ work would be done after he is dead, so even if he dies at Blunder’s hand, they won’t really mind.
As for the demon generals, they used this time to find what was making the Bone Blood Cult so confident.
There had to be something that made them believe they could handle everyone here.
"Now beg, show me your best performance.
Watch and plead as you watch everyone you care for die at my hands, haaah~ so exciting." Blunder said in a rather perverse tone, as the bloody hand grabbed the carriage.
Blunder had one of his hands raised as he grabbed the empty air while his eyes were fixed on Vritra’s expression, waiting to see that change—the change to satisfy his twisted desires.
As the carriage rose high into the air, the coachman jumped off hastily and ran towards the other carriage, praying to every god there is to survive this disaster.
He was an ordinary man in his fifties.
CREAAAKKKKK
The carriage began to shake wildly under the pressure of the bloody hand.
Vritra’s eyes widened in shock as he raised both hands and formed a hand of dust just as big in size.
Blunder’s face twisted even more in satisfaction as he sensed the desperation in Vritra’s action.
But the dust hand crumbled the moment it struck the hand of blood—the power difference was too big.
"Sigh, fine, go ahead and do it, you monster." Vritra just turned his gaze away from the gruesome scene that was about to follow.
He couldn’t bring himself to watch such destruction.
"Hmm..." Blunder raised an eyebrow, not expecting him to give up so easily.
He tilted his head slightly and exerted some pressure, as the carriage began to bend and a loud creaking and thudding sound was produced.
But Vritra still didn’t react.
He only clenched his fists and shut his eyes tight, enduring the pain.
BANG
Blunder exerted more force as the carriage was crushed and everything inside it became rubble.
The barrier that Yasmine had formed over it was destroyed as well.
"..." Blunder waited for the painful cries to come, but there was utter silence.
Finally, he locked his senses on the broken carriage—and there wasn’t a single drop of blood nor any corpses inside.
He looked back at the two men who had been ordered to follow Vritra.
The level of these two people was also well above two thousand, so there was absolutely no way they would make any mistake.
"Come forward." He said after letting go of the carriage, which fell down with a loud boom.
The luxurious carriage was destroyed just like that.
"Y-Yes sir." The two men in red clothes were shivering; they were even more baffled.
From the moment Vritra had left the temple, they had kept an eye on him all the way up to here, not missing a single moment.
The three women had been with him until this morning when he opened the windows, but now there was no one inside.
"Did the carriage disappear from your sight for even a moment?" Blunder asked, his tone emotionless.
But rage was building up inside him.
He was about to enjoy such a good show—but now it was gone just like that.
"N-NO sir, we kept watch over him the entire time.
We didn’t take a break for even a moment." One of the two men knelt in the air before the other followed.
They were crazy, but not nearly as much as Blunder.
"Hmm, I see.
Good job.
You deserve an award.

So right under your noses, this weak little toy who hasn’t even arrived at the legion rank yet made the three fully grown women disappear, and you had no idea about it?" Blunder asked, his lips stretching into a kind smile.
"S-Sir, all this time we didn’t n-notice any kind of change.
The carriages progressed just as usual.
At one point, one of the carriages did separate from the others, but I got rid of it and made sure no one was inside it.
I really d-don’t understand when it happened." One of the two men explained.
"Sigh, you are lucky.
If this wasn’t such an important occasion, then I would have dealt with you both first.
Stand up and return to your positions.
Your punishment will come soon." Blunder waved his hand as the two men took their positions.

’From what I have seen of him, he would have definitely beaten the two to a pulp for making such a big mistake—yet he didn’t right now, which means he needs them all for his next plan, and they need to be at certain positions...’ Vritra pondered, an unusual habit of his to observe the surroundings.
But he soon gave up.
It wouldn’t matter what he thinks or plans, those people are way too strong and no trick would work against them.
If he really wished to beat them right now, then he probably would need to be born again.
"Sigh, that took away all the fun.
I thought before the actual battle I could have a delicious appetizer, but I guess you are too smart—" Blunder shook his head.
He was quite impressed by Vritra’s capability and felt more reluctant to just directly kill him.
Wouldn’t it be much better to slowly kill this great toy?
And he might really get the chance to kill those women in front of him in the future.
But Blunder’s words were interrupted by Vritra’s loud shout:
"You think you can scare me just because you are a bit stronger?
If you weren’t born so long before me then you would be nothing in front of me.
Just wait—I’m going to kill you with my hands."
"Wait, what are you planning to do?
You can’t fight them.
I am going to create a disturbance in the barrier now, and then you could escape through the hole." Yasmine spoke.
She gathered all her energy, even her soul energy, to create one powerful attack and blast a part of the barrier.
’Heh, don’t think you can just escape from your debt so easily.
You owe me so many spanks.
Before I take my revenge for all the teasing, I am not going to let you leave.

chapters.title: Chapter 154: Blunder’s Blunder
paragraphs: After locking Yasmine away, Vritra took a deep breath. Even with his plan, the chances of his survival were quite low, but that seemed to be the only way.
He ignored the constant messages of the sin points he was gaining. Right now, that was the furthest thing he wanted to focus on, even if the number of sin points was quite large.

Vritra’s body rose into the air as a large dust storm formed in the surroundings. He didn’t plan to reveal any of his hidden cards—like Bob or many of his great skills—that would only increase his chances of dying.

Faceless gestured for all his men to move to the corner of the barrier. They were only here to fill the empty ranks in the Dunshire kingdom. They weren’t here for the fight but got caught up because of the Bone Blood Cult.
Blunder also gestured for his group to move further, but instead of moving in a random direction, all of them seemed to have pre-determined positions. They were definitely here with a purpose.

The great battle was finally starting, and it seemed it would start with the sacrifice of Vritra by the hands of the Bone Blood Cult—the cultists who love offering sacrifices to the god they believe in.

"You are dumber than I thought, going brute against me..." Blunder shook his head, losing a little interest in Vritra, but still a bit hopeful. He wondered if this young boy had any kind of special means to protect himself.
Vritra didn’t care about anything. He exhausted a large amount of his energy as he formed a large sword with the dust and kept condensing it into a more compact form, making it extremely sharp.
Even if he was going down, that wouldn’t happen without a fight. His task was pretty easy—just to get himself killed. How hard could that be? What could go wrong?

Just get killed, remain a corpse for the entire battle, and then get revived after everyone leaves. It would be very painful and maybe a bit scary, but Vritra wondered how it would feel to die. Using the barbaric attack, he wished to get himself killed in one strike.
Blunder just watched Vritra prepare his attack. This was a strong move... but for someone of his level, to strong people like them, it was nothing more than a tap with a soft leaf.

Vritra condensed a large sword that was dozens of meters long and extremely sharp. With a thunderous roar, he shot forward while at the same time, the sword descended on top of Blunder, who just stood there calmly.
BOOOOOM!!

In the two armies, all the men below the rank of Legion were quite surprised by that attack. That attack shouldn’t be possible with his current level. Even the mana used was too large, but in the end, it was still useless.

Vritra struck Blunder’s chest with all his might—of course, without the use of ’Shift’. His muscles were bulging, but the moment his fist struck Blunder, aside from a loud sound, there was no effect at all. The entire force was just absorbed by Blunder’s muscles.

"Haa. What a disappointment, and here I thought you were better than that. Why couldn’t you have entertained me for a bit longer? Looks like, in the face of death, even you can’t make rational decisions," Blunder spoke as he saw the shock visible over Vritra’s face.

"Well, I have already wasted enough time. I can’t make my guests wait any longer, so let’s end this game right here..." Blunder’s face twisted into an unsightly grin as his lips spread wide, before he added: "for now, that is."

Before Vritra could react, Blunder lightly slapped Vritra’s chest with the back of his hand. Casually, a blood energy consumed his body before he was thrown back toward the ground at lightning speed, becoming a blur before he struck the ground and his body was embedded in a deep crater.
COUGH COUGH
Vritra’s vision became hazy.

Every bone in his body had been shattered and the skin all over his body was torn. His blood seemed to be affected by that red energy as it transformed into some sort of acid and began to burn his body from the inside.

Since Blunder had decided not to kill Vritra instantly, that was why he survived just barely. But even with his healing skill and Shift working in the background, the condition of his body got worse and worse.
He was so close to death—yet just one step away. Vritra couldn’t do anything. Even his brain was severely damaged and his energy reserves had been disrupted, injuring him in the process.
His vitality dropped rapidly from 100% to less than 3% in an instant and continued to decrease. He was barely breathing, but each breath brought a wave of pain along with it.

The pain and injury he got upon swallowing the demon lord’s core seemed like a joke at this moment. Vritra couldn’t even feel most of his body, and he stared at the sky with a hazy red vision, completely unaware of what was happening around him.

He just lay in the crater like a corpse. Because of Blunder’s twisted personality, the very first step seemed to have failed. Blunder wanted Vritra to suffer more, so he didn’t kill Vritra instantly, but sent him almost to death’s door.
"Now that he is taken care of, shall we start our business?" After looking at the broken Vritra with satisfaction, Blunder looked at the five men from the Nine Pacts and the three demon generals.

"Tell me, are you the one who stole our core?" Silquor asked, quickly forgetting about what had just transpired. None of them were good people, so they wouldn’t care about anyone insignificant. If they weren’t in such a bad mood, they might even have enjoyed the pathetic death of a pathetic human.
"Hahaha. And what if I am? What are you going to do?" Blunder asked arrogantly, placing his hands over his waist and puffing his chest, making fun of the demon general Thaddeus.
"Before we start, let me finish him," Faceless said while looking at Vritra. After all, that was their task, and it was better to kill him now than to watch him suffer in pain before he died.
They weren’t like the Bone Blood Cult who enjoyed murdering others. They had a goal, and they did whatever it took to achieve it.
Vritra’s condition was already so bad, there was barely any life left in him; he was far too broken that just a light nudge might send him to the afterlife.

"Try it if you can. And since he is already here, why don’t we let him watch our epic fight? He will be able to go to the afterworld with such a great memory—what could be a better parting gift for someone like him?" Blunder laughed as he saw Vritra’s barely open eyes. He was finally enjoying this.
For the first time in his life, Blunder made a blunder that he would only come to know about—and regret—after a short time.
A blunder that made him have nightmares for the remaining period of his life, changed his personality greatly, and broke him completely.
The regret of not killing Vritra directly and just letting Vritra continue with his plan.

chapters.title: Chapter 155: Grievances
paragraphs: Faceless stared at Vritra for a few seconds, his body was completely disfigured and bruised; it was impossible to tell that it was the same handsome boy that charged at Blunder fearlessly moments ago.

He sighed and decided to let Blunder fulfill his wishes, he wasn’t new to torturing people after all, so it didn’t affect him at all. Vritra would be dead in just a few more minutes at max, until then he would hang on the thin line between life and death, suffering through a hellish pain.
While the red energy that entered his body made his body rot, that was one of the worst deaths one could receive.
Ignoring the dying Vritra on the ground, they all finally turned their attention to one another—the main fight was about to begin.
"Now, answer me, Faceless, did you have anything to do with the stealing of the core?" Morvik asked. His voice seemed even sharper in his insect form, making the ears of the two armies hurt.
"Yes. I was only informed about it by the Bone Blood Cult. My goal in coming to this kingdom this time was just to kill that boy. And now my task has been completed.
I have nothing to do with that core of yours, so I would advise you not to go against the Nine Pacts. It is better to have more friends than more enemies," Faceless said in an emotionless tone.
Now that Vritra was almost dead, he could return and the work of Nine Pacts in this kingdom would continue just like before, with the new batches of people.

"Hmm. You will have to wait here until I have taken care of this crazy insect. I hope you aren’t lying to me right now, otherwise if you are... not even the Nine Pacts will be able to save you," Thaddeus warned, before fixing his sight on Blunder and the nine other men beside him.

"You focus on him, while I and Silquor will take care of the nine others," Morvik spoke as he pointed at Blunder. In terms of strength, they could easily kill all ten of the people, but it seemed those Bone Blood Cult lunatics had planned something big in advance. They dared to take so many people at once, after all.

"Hahaha. It’s about to get so much fun. Are you watching this, Vritra? Don’t die yet and keep watching, at least your death will be worth it," Blunder spoke as he spread his arms in the air and seemed to have gone crazy with his wild laughter.

Soon the other men from Bone Blood Cult—over ten thousand men—began laughing similarly, confusing Faceless and the three demon generals. These lunatics were acting too strange, so the demon generals decided to act fast while Faceless just decided to wait at the side and observe the situation.
Though he might need to join the battle very soon.
ROOOAAAAAARRRRRRRRRRRR

Thaddeus let out an ear-piercing roar, his bull-like face full of rage and his long round horns glowing with an even brighter light. Then he kicked the air, creating a huge blast as his body shot forward at such a speed that barely a very few people could even track him.
FUUOOOOOOOOOO

Thaddeus’s body tore through the air as he flashed in front of Blunder. Without saying a word, he shot out a punch. Of course, they had greatly restricted their strength and didn’t dare to use anything above level two thousand, or they might attract some very annoying and dangerous people.

Blunder didn’t back down. While laughing maniacally, he opened his mouth wide—so wide that his cheeks began to tear. Then a blood-red liquid flooded out of his mouth, instantly forming a huge blood wall in front of him.
BOOOOOOOOOM!!

The fist of the large bull collided with the blood wall and it instantly exploded into tiny pieces, but that was enough time for Blunder to dodge. He looked at Thaddeus with a mocking smile as he jumped backward twice and seemed to have arrived at just the right spot.
The other two demon generals also rushed towards the nine men, but the latter just stood rooted to their positions—as if leaving their positions was scarier than getting killed by those monsters.
"EVERYONE, START!!" Blunder gave a loud shout as everyone’s hearts trembled with anticipation. They were right—he indeed had some plan.

Yasmine, who had been locked in a dark space by Vritra, suddenly froze. She sensed the changes the moment Vritra was struck. She let out an agonizing cry and felt herself break. Yasmine could feel how weak Vritra was right now and how close to death he must be.
Her heart was breaking but she couldn’t do anything. She understood what his plan exactly was. The dragon queen cried, feeling so much pain in her heart.

Yasmine just wanted to go out and rip everyone present there to shreds, to protect her love. She felt so powerless as she could only watch the person she loved the most—the only person she cared so much about—die slowly.
Even with that revival potion, she didn’t want her husband to suffer so much. He was just a normal human some time ago and now he had to go through all this just to survive; it was too cruel.

A long distance away, inside a small carriage, Fiona, Diana, and Vanessa were sitting with emotionless faces in complete silence. They had separated from Vritra earlier in the day and then continued their journey in this carriage that they bought separately.
On Vanessa’s side, Zengis was sitting along with Bobby. The two were there to protect them at all costs, but Vanessa thought it was more of a symbolic thing.
To bring them out of that carriage under the gazes of those two people, Vritra used the same trick he used when making the announcer from that guard competition disappear at the end.
By sending them into the earth—but without Yasmine’s barrier that blocked their senses, it wouldn’t have been possible.

He broke a part of the carriage’s floor. When the speed of the carriage became slow, Vritra manipulated the ground and, inside the forest with high vegetation, made a very deep hole in the ground that swallowed the three women, and they were able to get out without getting noticed.

The three women were just waiting for Vritra’s return. Before sending them away, he had told them that someone was following them. So he sent them away first and said he would return after losing those people tailing them, but there were still no signs of him.
Suddenly, Vanessa’s and Diana’s eyes widened as they sensed the ominous change. Their eyes widened and, unconsciously, they both looked at one another—the horror evident.
Of course, Diana wasn’t as terrified as Vanessa. Vritra’s mother felt her body go numb as she felt a shiver. She knew that her son was in extreme danger and was currently very close to death.
"HONEYYYY!!" Vanessa stood up abruptly, startling Fiona, her eyes filling with tears as she tried to rush out of the carriage, but was stopped by Diana, who was tasked by Vritra to keep her safe.
’So he knew this was going to happen,’ Diana thought as she worriedly glanced into the sky while trying to stop Vanessa, who seemed to have gone mad.

The dragon queen cried, feeling so much pain in her heart.
Yasmine just wanted to go out and rip everyone present there to shreds, to protect her love.
She felt so powerless as she could only watch the person she loved the most—the only person she cared so much about—die slowly.
Even with that revival potion, she didn’t want her husband to suffer so much.
He was just a normal human some time ago and now he had to go through all this just to survive; it was too cruel.
A long distance away, inside a small carriage, Fiona, Diana, and Vanessa were sitting with emotionless faces in complete silence.
They had separated from Vritra earlier in the day and then continued their journey in this carriage that they bought separately.
On Vanessa’s side, Zengis was sitting along with Bobby.
The two were there to protect them at all costs, but Vanessa thought it was more of a symbolic thing.
To bring them out of that carriage under the gazes of those two people, Vritra used the same trick he used when making the announcer from that guard competition disappear at the end.
By sending them into the earth—but without Yasmine’s barrier that blocked their senses, it wouldn’t have been possible.
He broke a part of the carriage’s floor.

When the speed of the carriage became slow, Vritra manipulated the ground and, inside the forest with high vegetation, made a very deep hole in the ground that swallowed the three women, and they were able to get out without getting noticed.
The three women were just waiting for Vritra’s return.
Before sending them away, he had told them that someone was following them.
So he sent them away first and said he would return after losing those people tailing them, but there were still no signs of him.
Suddenly, Vanessa’s and Diana’s eyes widened as they sensed the ominous change.
Their eyes widened and, unconsciously, they both looked at one another—the horror evident.
Of course, Diana wasn’t as terrified as Vanessa.
Vritra’s mother felt her body go numb as she felt a shiver.
She knew that her son was in extreme danger and was currently very close to death.
"HONEYYYY!!" Vanessa stood up abruptly, startling Fiona, her eyes filling with tears as she tried to rush out of the carriage, but was stopped by Diana, who was tasked by Vritra to keep her safe.
’So he knew this was going to happen,’ Diana thought as she worriedly glanced into the sky while trying to stop Vanessa, who seemed to have gone mad.

chapters.title: Chapter 156: Larva
paragraphs: HUFF HUFF
Vritra’s breathing was extremely weak, he was clearly very close to death. Maybe his plan really might succeed in the end, but he would have preferred a quicker death rather than this.

His half-lidded eyes stared blankly at the sky, his mind had stopped working and he couldn’t form a single thought; it was like countless red images were flashing in front of him, but Vritra had no idea what was happening around him or to him.

In the sky, all the people dressed in red from the Bone Blood Cult took out thousands of exactly same-looking red-colored cubes—the Glyphs. Vritra continued to see the scene that was tinged with redness in his eyes. The demon generals and the Nine Pacts seemed to be very shocked.
Over ten thousand people poured their energies into those fist-sized cubes. Although both the demon generals and Nine Pacts tried to stop the change, it was useless.

Vritra’s vitality, instead of increasing with his skills, continued to plummet with each passing moment. As he lost complete control over his body, the Demon Lord’s core that was forcefully stored in his body finally had a chance to get out of there.

It began to release vast amounts of energy, out of which only a little was able to leak out of the barrier and the Evil-Veyll God Essence Core. But just that amount began to destroy his body even further.

Vritra had no control over anything. Although he had never used theSwitchskill before because it was too dangerous and probably had the function of releasing that Demon Lord’s energy, without any control over it, using that skill was nothing short of suicide.

ButSwitchwas a hybrid skill—its passive part was like a bomb. In a situation like the present one where he had no control over his own body, it could be activated forcefully and the core would then erupt.
So instead of a usable skill,Switchwas more like a prison for the Demon Lord’s core. But finally, it was slowly breaking that prison.
Vritra couldn’t care less about anything right now. As his health dropped below 2%, he felt as if the world was spinning, and his sight had slowly started to darken.

He continued to look at the sky. Vritra couldn’t hear anything, but in those blurry images, the shock on the faces of the demon generals and the Nine Pacts was evident, as another barrier covered the whole place.

The people in the sky were shouting, but Vritra’s world was slowly approaching stillness and silence. His health soon got below 1%, and finally, Vritra drifted into unconsciousness as everything became silent—with no pain.
And then...
[Health has reached the critical point.]
[Elegy Parasite Activated!!]
In the next moment, a black tattoo rapidly began to manifest on his back.

A coiled, pale larva with spiny ridges and a gaping, hook-like mouth took form on his body, spreading across his entire back. Its head appeared nestled below Vritra’s neck, locked in place almost as if it had "bitten" into his body.
Faint vein-like lines spread from it across Vritra’s entire body—those vein-like tattoos appearing all over his skin. The scene looked as if the parasite was feeding off of him.
Just as the parasite was activated, Vritra’s eyes opened suddenly—and everything was drowned in pure darkness. His pupils, sclera—everything was covered by pitch black.
Then, a flurry of messages poured in front of him.
[Chances of survival: 0.0001%]

The parasite didn’t act immediately. It began to search for the most optimal solution to achieve its goal of survival at any cost. The body was too damaged and couldn’t move. After scanning his body, it assessed the surroundings and every possible route that could allow it to survive.
Elegy Parasitewould use every resource or ability available to survive—no matter what needed to be sacrificed, even if it was his humanity or even their lives.

After just a single moment, theElegy Parasitehad found the path with the highest possibility of survival. Then it began to plan things out. The entire process took no more than a second—the others hadn’t even noticed any of the changes that were occurring on his body.

The black veins that spread across his entire body, or his pitch-black eyes that were staring at the sky emotionlessly—Vritra had disappeared for now, and his mind at this point was more like a machine with the highest possible efficiency.
Finally, after two seconds had passed and there was barely a little vitality left in his body, theElegy Parasitelocked onto the wisps of demonic energy leaking into his body and wreaking havoc.
Then...
[Switch Activated.]
[Switch: Demonification (1%)]
Elegy Parasiteallowed the furious demonic core a small window to leak exactly 1% of its energy, as it flooded out and almost tore him apart.

The demonic energy, flesh, and blood might not hurt Vritra’s body as much as they would hurt others, but neither could his body handle that amount of energy nor that concentration. Even for him, it began to act like acidic poison.

In the sky, the three demon generals and the men from the Nine Pacts were shocked to find themselves trapped by that restricting barrier. It would reduce the levels of anyone trapped inside to be around 1500 to 1600.
"H- How did you obtain that? Is the Bone Blood Cult now colluding with them?" Silquor asked in bafflement, his eyes wide open.
"Bone Blood Cult, do you really plan to go against all the humans? What is the meaning of this? The Nine Pacts will make your cult disappear!!" Faceless shouted, his body burning with rage.
Aside from demons and all the other races, there are other creatures that stand against all life forms—they hurt humans, demons, dragons, and every other race alike.

"Hahaha, what does it matter? If all the witnesses disappear, then it never existed." Then with an arrogant look he spoke: "And don’t count me with the likes of you. We from the Bone Blood Cult have far surpassed humanity and the restrictions of you small life forms. Demons, humans—they’re all just lowly creatures compared to us."

The demon generals and Nine Pacts’ blood boiled at those words. They wanted to kill those psychos, but feeling the restrictions over their bodies, they held back. Fighting in Bone Blood Cult’s domain would be highly disadvantageous for them.
Just as the fight seemed about to break out, a terrifying energy erupted from the crater on the ground—shocking every single person present in the barrier.

Even the barrier set up by Bone Blood Cult couldn’t restrict this energy. They all sensed the extreme demonic energy and were shocked by the intensity of this sudden eruption. The most shocked, of course, were the three demon generals, who recognized this energy instantly.
"I- Isn’t that the energy of our lord? Why is that coming from there?" Morvik spoke in confusion.
"It’s coming from that human... he was so weak. How could this be?" Faceless mumbled in bewilderment.
The energy of the Demon Lord instantly spread all across Vritra’s body, filling each and every cell in his body—destroying everything and bringing him closer to death with each passing moment.

chapters.title: Chapter 157: THUMP!! THUMP!!
paragraphs: Everyone on the battlefield was shocked by the explosion of the demonic energy. They all stared at Vritra, whose body had been almost destroyed by the destructive force.

It was obvious that Vritra was the one who had the Demon Lord’s core in his body. None among the three generals could believe that such a weak person was able to store something so powerful—and he even managed to do so in less than a minute.
They all looked at Blunder, thinking that he must be behind this as well, but upon seeing the shock on his face, it was obvious that even he had no idea about it.

Thaddeus just wanted to rush forward and take back that core, but right now it seemed that the energy core was going berserk after being trapped for some time. Everyone was afraid that if that thing exploded, none of them would be able to survive.

Although only 1% of its energy was leaking at this moment, it began to destroy Vritra’s body at an extremely high pace. The Elegy Parasite, which had spread itself across Vritra’s entire body, seemed to be suffering as well.

The tattoo on his back was being torn as, slowly, Vritra’s body began to wither and break apart. While this process was continuing, the others could only watch this scene in anticipation, waiting to see the outcome.
All of them moved back in haste, ready to leave the area as fast as possible if something went wrong.
Nine Pacts and the demon generals wanted to move even further back, but they were trapped in there by the barrier formed by Blunder.

While Blunder also wanted to move away, he himself was trapped by his own barrier and couldn’t remove it. It wouldn’t be activated again easily, and if removed, then the two other parties would surely kill them all.

More than fifty percent of Vritra’s body was destroyed within moments, and his health was close to 0. Just at that moment, a bottle was thrown toward the sky—not too high, but enough to create a little distance.

All the others swept their senses over the bottle and were shocked by the life force contained in that small glass bottle. It was a mythical treasure—something that could even bring the dead back to life.

They were all tempted to rush forward to catch it, but the fear of the Demon Lord’s energy kept them at bay. They could only watch as the bottle reached a height of over twenty feet before it began to fall down toward Vritra.
While inside the crater, the Demon Lord’s energy had mostly destroyed Vritra’s body, and then...
Finally, his vitality reached 0.
His breathing stopped completely, and his heart was dissolved into nothingness. He was lost into oblivion.
He was finally dead—and the first to notice this change were none other than Yasmine, Vanessa, and Diana.
Out of the three women, the former two completely broke down when they could no longer feel his presence. They couldn’t believe that... Vritra was dead.
Their connection with Vritra, on every possible level, went very deep. And the moment they sensed his death, the two women received such a heavy shock that they both fainted almost at the same time.
Morvik stared at the disbelieving scene in shock—nothing seemed to be making sense. So Vritra ended up getting killed by the treasure he stole; almost his entire body had been reduced to nothing.
In the crater, only his disfigured head, neck, and a part of his torso remained—which were also being destroyed with each passing moment.

"He was killed by the Demon Lord’s energy... how did all this happen? It just doesn’t make any sense! How did he even obtain it?" Silquor roared out loud. The risk of the explosion had just increased after Vritra’s death.

The three generals glanced to the other side and saw the greed in Blunder and Faceless’s eyes. They too wanted to get the Demon Lord’s core. As soon as the core calmed down, a fight would break out—and the winner would get the core.
CRACK

Finally, they came out of their shock as they watched the glass bottle fall over Vritra’s body. The glass was instantly shattered by the dark bluish energy, as the glistening liquid inside spread across the remainder of Vritra’s body.

The destructive energy attacked even the liquid, but it wasn’t able to do anything. At first, the glistening liquid just fell over his body like a normal liquid. And in the next moment, as if locking onto him, all the liquid was sucked inside his battered body.
[Consumed Pulse Reversal!!]

Then, under several tens of thousands of eyes, a strong life energy filled Vritra’s body—and an internal conflict began. The demonic energy was destroying his body while the potion was healing him rapidly. Not just his body—his mind and soul as well.

The struggle between the two entities continued for a few seconds, but in the end, the Demon Lord’s energy was defeated by the Pulse Reversal potion. Instead, it began to devour all its energy to create Vritra’s new body.
Every bit of energy that was leaking out of the demonic core was instantly sucked by the potion, which soon covered Vritra’s body in a sparkling sheet.
It was a miraculous sight of rebirth—his body was being built from nothing.
Veins, bones, muscles—everything began to form under the bright sparkling sheet that wrapped around him and formed the shape of a body.
All the people present were seeing such a scene for the first time. They were simply frozen in awe and did not think for a moment to do anything.
Every energy present in Vritra’s body—his mana, Demon Lord’s energy, Evil Veyll God essence, and so on—all of it was being used to construct his new body.

Except for the sound of twisting and the formation of Vritra’s body, the entire battlefield was completely silent. The demonic energy continued to struggle, but the more energy it drew from the core, the more of it was sucked away.
Vritra’s limbs, torso, and so on slowly began to form. The whole process of his body formation took a bit over five minutes—the Pulse Reversal potion was too amazing.
THUMP THUMP
Less than ten minutes had passed when Vritra’s newly formed hearts thumped for the first time. It was like his body was electrocuted, as his body jerked suddenly before becoming still again.

Purple blood veins bulged and became visible under his pale white skin as the two hearts began to pump blood all across his body. Soon, the new nerves connected with the brain and began to send electric signals—and the brain started working once again.

Vritra sucked in a very deep breath, filling his lungs to the brim with air. Then his breathing returned to normal. Slowly, every function of his body restarted and returned to its normal state—but that "normal" state seemed to be completely different from before.
The glistening thin sheet slowly disappeared as his body became visible—unscathed and brand new, vastly different both internally and externally.
The moment he came back to life,Switchgot to work and once again locked away the Demon Lord’s core, as Vritra lay in the crater... still unconscious.

chapters.title: Chapter 158: Demon
paragraphs: Finally, Vritra’s body was formed, and it had completely surpassed its peak state. The Demon Lord’s energy was locked away, and he lay unconscious in the crater.
With a jolt, everyone seemed to come out of their trance-like state, as some shook their heads and others rubbed their eyes at such a scene—watching a person actually come back from the dead.
Not just that, after the rebirth, it seemed his body had completely transformed and he no longer looked like a human.
There were two horns over his head, his skin looking even more pale and smooth, and his muscles more refined. His black hair had grown longer.
"He has the core in his body—we have to take it back," Silquor spoke in haste. The others planned to steal it, so they had to make the first move.
Vritra was very weak, and in his unconscious state, he was just waiting to be killed again after his rebirth. But right now, Blunder had the highest chances of obtaining it because of the barrier.

The three were in a state of stalemate. They looked at one another and waited for someone to make a move—after all, whoever moved first would have the least chance of obtaining the core and the highest chances of dying.
[Elegy Parasite awakened.]
Since the danger had not been removed yet, the parasite instantly continued with its plan. Now, everyone clearly saw those tiny vein-like black lines spreading all over Vritra’s body.
Then his eyes shot open, completely consumed by darkness. While watching this scene, everyone began to feel anxious—they were sure Vritra wasn’t awake, but then what was controlling him?
Then, under all the eyes, Vritra’s body slowly began to rise, as if being pulled by invisible strings; his torso was pulled up first as he rose in such an unnatural manner.
As Vritra got on his feet, his body slumped forward slightly. Then he straightened, his head tilted upwards, and took a long breath.

"Something is not right. How about we get rid of this anomaly first before we fight for the Demon Lord’s core?" Faceless suggested. Seeing those pitch-black eyes without a tinge of white, he had a bad feeling in his heart.
"Hah, what’s there to decide? That core belongs to us, so we will be the one to get it. Anyone who doesn’t think so will have to prove their resolve with their lives," Thaddeus roared.
"Stupid demon, this is not the time to fight among ourselves—we have to remove that unpredictable factor first," Faceless added, feeling frustrated.
"Hey, don’t forget to let me join in the fun. Whatever you are planning to do, I would be the end winner anyway—hahahaha!"

Blunder shot his head back and laughed. He didn’t take Vritra seriously at all. He believed that if he could kill Vritra once, then he could do so a second, third, fourth, and as many times as he wanted.
While the major parties were busy chattering, another change began to take place in the crater.
[Switch Activated.]
[Switch: Demonification (1%)]

Instantly, demonic energy flooded out of the core and entered his body. But unlike before, it was no longer like a poison to him. Vritra’s body had completely transformed. Every organ, cell, bone—everything had changed into something that didn’t exist.
Something that shouldn’t exist.

But even at 1%, the energy of the Demon Lord was still very potent, while Vritra’s level was too low. Normally it would have still been harmful to him, but as the demonic energy flowed through his blood and veins—

Both the hearts began to work rapidly as they pumped that energy and channelled it all over his body. A dark purplish mist began to rise from his body as his veins glowed and seemed to be under intense pressure.

His aura rose quickly, instantly surpassing the Legion rank within moments. The entire space inside the barrier seemed to be consumed by that aura. The sudden change caught everyone off guard, and they were shocked that Vritra was actually able to use the energy of a Demon Lord. He was no longer human.
Aside from the top powers, all of the thousands of men suffocated under the dense pressure. Vritra looked more like a demon than those demon generals—especially with those pitch-black, hollow eyes.
A sense of danger spread across the whole place. The sound of Vritra’s two hearts thumping could be heard as, within moments, his body seemed to have undergone a major change.
"Fuck, he is going to—" Faceless was just shouting when Vritra suddenly disappeared from his position, his presence completely gone from the battlefield.
Even though he was being controlled by that parasite right now, it could make use of every ability available to him—whether it be Fourth Dimension, Suck! Suck! Suck!, or anything else.
The five men in black clothes from the Nine Pacts became vigilant and scanned the surroundings but couldn’t find him anywhere.

Vritra’s agility had surpassed most of the people present in this space. He didn’t target the Bone Blood Cult first—after all, they were keeping up the barrier, which would provide a benefit to him by making everyone else weaker.
FWOOSH

The first man among the five from Nine Pacts suddenly felt something lightly touching his head as Vritra appeared behind him. His right hand was raised, and he placed the tips of the five fingers gently over his head.

It was as if time itself had paused for a moment. The first man had just sensed Vritra’s presence and was filled with a dreadful feeling. This was too absurd—he shouldn’t even be Legion ranked, and all of a sudden he was displaying such a level of combat.
TAP

His pinky finger was raised slightly, and then he tapped over his head. With a loud crunching sound, his neck twisted, and the man’s head was rotated by a complete 180°. His face held a terrified expression as he finally got to look at the emotionless face of the demon.
His neck twisted with a sickening crack, spinning all the way around.

Bone pierced through the skin at the base, tendons snapped like cords, and torn veins sprayed blood across Vritra’s body—only to disappear upon coming into contact with the purple aura rising around his body. His head hung backward, eyes wide open with shock and fear.

Killing people who had reached the Legion rank is extremely difficult. Even if their heads are cut off, they won’t die so easily—especially people who had reached the 2nd Legion rank or 3rd Legion rank, or in other words, people over level two thousand or three thousand and so on.

It was even more difficult to kill them. Even if their body is destroyed, they would survive. Just take Yasmine, for example, who was able to survive even after her body was destroyed and her soul was severely injured—but her level was exceptionally high.
The five people who had followed Faceless here all had levels between two thousand to three thousand. They were all at the 2nd Legion rank.
BOOOOM!!

So even though the first man’s neck was twisted, he still wasn’t dead. Vritra lightly squeezed his fingers—and the man’s head exploded instantly, creating a bloody cloud of flesh, blood, and brain pieces.

With a jolt, everyone seemed to come out of their trance-like state, as some shook their heads and others rubbed their eyes at such a scene—watching a person actually come back from the dead.

chapters.title: Chapter 159: Origin: Unknown
paragraphs: Upon Vritra’s death, the number of people had been reduced by one, but upon his rebirth, the number of demons inside the barrier had increased.
Despite becoming a demon, his body was still incapable of constantly using so much energy. ButElegy Parasitepushed his limits and even began to extract Vritra’s life force to keep him going.
BOOOOOM!!

With a loud boom, the head of the man from the Nine Pacts exploded as his body limply began to fall toward the ground. Of course, he wasn’t dead yet, but that was a fatal injury and would need some time to heal on its own.
Hearing that loud sound, everyone seemed to be filled with a feeling of trepidation. The next moment, Vritra disappeared once again, baffling everyone.

"Remove this fucking barrier, otherwise all of us are going to die here together! We can’t handle our Lord’s energy with so little strength, you Bone Blood Cult bastards!" Silquor roared in rage and frustration. He felt immense anger at seeing someone else use that essence core.
Then Vritra’s body flashed again. He appeared in front of the army of over ten thousand men from the Nine Pacts, who had moved to the back of the barrier, holding the giant axes in both his hands.

While a devastating storm of dust rose into the air—thousands of times more powerful and dangerous than before—it swallowed all the people. And as the particles brushed against their bodies, their skin was torn and began to bleed.

The fearful images of thousands of men were reflected in Vritra’s black eyes. His body left behind an afterimage as he swung both axes in a horizontal slash, tearing through the bodies of dozens of Nine Pacts members.
All the people here were much stronger than the ones that Vritra had slaughtered back in that tomb, but in his current form, they didn’t even have the time to react as their bodies were torn in two.
Then...

[You have killed a Level 769 Human.]
[You have killed a Level 402 Human.]
[You have killed a Level 536 Human.]
[+EXP Earned.]
[You have Levelled Up!]
[You have Levelled Up!]
[You have Levelled Up!]
[All Stats Increased by 1.]

[You have gained 1 Allocation Point.]

Vritra was like a raging fire in a thick forest—wherever his body moved, he left behind a trail of torn corpses. There was no technique but pure and utter violence. His speed had risen to such a level that by the time the Nine Pacts’ men noticed him, he had already slaughtered more than a hundred men.

His body kept flashing in all directions. There were no screams—just pure terror. None among the top leaders from the Nine Pacts were able to come help, as they were all struggling against the deadly storm that was manifested using the destructive demonic energy.
"H-He is here, get in the formation and—"

A cloud of blood rose in the sky. Vritra’s face was completely expressionless. A bloody mist filled the air. He was killing them all like a machine. With each slash of his axe, their bodies were dismembered and thrown to the ground.

Messages after messages poured in front of him. If he was conscious, Vritra would have been shocked that he was actually receiving experience points upon killing humans—which directly meant that even his origins were no longer that of humans.
He had completely transformed into a demon—no, something far more abnormal, a very unique and strange mutation or evolution.
ADemonic Dragon, but also excessively different from both.

Raising his hands high, Vritra threw both his weapons forward with all his strength. The men were either cut down or turned into minced meat upon colliding with them. The axes charged through the crowd without any hindrance at all.

"Remove this darned barrier! If this goes on, with our limited strength, we won’t be able to fight him. He will soon kill all my army—and then it will be your turn!" Faceless shouted, while protecting himself against the sneak attacks being launched by the purplish dust.

"Hah! I can kill him again. I will do it right this time. There is no way he could handle this level of power for long. And the moment he returns to his weak body, I will tear him to pieces with my own hands. Till then, just wait patiently for your turn." Blunder screamed. The thing he hated most was letting his targets live a happy and peaceful life.
But seeing Vritra so high and mighty in the sky, as he massacred hundreds of people with each passing moment, Blunder felt an even stronger wish to kill him—to see him suffer.
"Tch. That twisted bastard... What about you? Can you do anything?" Faceless was going mad as he watched so many of his men dying. He looked at the three demon generals and asked.

"H-How can he do that? How can he control our Lord’s energy and core? It is still too much for him to handle—and his body is already starting to reach its limits. But that’s only because his level is still too low." Morvik mumbled in shock. The three generals were all baffled.
They could tell that Vritra was now a demon—and no ordinary demon at that. They clearly heard the sound of two hearts from his body.
Even their Lord wasn’t as special. Only a few Demon Lords had two hearts, and that number could be counted on the fingers of one hand—and a finger or two might still be left.

Though it was highly possible among the Demon Gods. According to the rumors, they all possess two hearts. So it was impossible to understand how Vritra’s body underwent such a mutation. It wasn’t just because of that potion. Aside from their Demon Lord’s core, Vritra definitely possessed something even more valuable and powerful.
"We have to get his body and find the answers," Thaddeus spoke. But with their levels locked, they were busy just keeping themselves safe.
Faceless saw the tranced demon generals and knew no help would be coming from them. He gritted his teeth and could only watch as his army was getting slaughtered by that demon.
BAANNNGGGGG!!
BAANNNGGGGG!!

Flesh splattered everywhere. The two large weapons cleared two straight lines through the large army as they cleaved through bodies, killing hundreds of men. Most of them panicked and began to run away, while a few confident ones—who believed in numbers—rushed forward to attack Vritra, who was in that strange state.
And the result?
BOOOOOOOOOM!!
Just by punching the empty air, a strong shockwave was created that made their bodies explode upon impact.

The purplish aura churning around his body grew denser and denser. His hearts were going all out to pump the Demon Lord’s energy across his body—constantly increasing his strength, while his body was working at full capacity.
Slaughtering the wave of humans at rapid speed, each strike resulted in the deaths of hundreds, as his level grew quickly.
In such a short time, Vritra had killed more than five thousand men. But he didn’t stop, nor did he slow down, as he continued with the annihilation.
